title: Read the Escape, Design the Next Drug

scenes.tts: In 2001 a capsule was approved for a leukaemia. It was aimed at one enzyme. But about five hundred human kinases hold A T P in nearly the same pocket. A kinase is an enzyme that moves a phosphate onto a protein. Around 1990, a molecule shaped to jam one pocket was expected to jam dozens. So how do you drug just one?
scenes.caption: In 2001 a capsule was approved for a leukaemia. It was aimed at one enzyme. But about five hundred human kinases hold ATP in nearly the same pocket. A kinase is an enzyme that moves a phosphate onto a protein. Around 1990, a molecule shaped to jam one pocket was expected to jam dozens. So how do you drug just one?
scenes.visual: A field of identical kinase blobs, each with the same pocket, with ATP chips in them; a drug wedge shaped for one pocket is expected to fit dozens (wedges spread to many), then a question mark over a single kinase.
scenes.narration: In 2001 a capsule was approved for a leukaemia. It was aimed at one enzyme. But about five hundred human kinases hold ATP in nearly the same pocket. A kinase is an enzyme that moves a phosphate onto a protein. Around 1990, a molecule shaped to jam one pocket was expected to jam dozens. So how do you drug just one?

scenes.tts: The molecule that worked is called imatinib. It hit a short list of kinases, not hundreds. One of them is B C R A B L. This fused kinase is always on, and it drives chronic myeloid leukaemia. Imatinib sits in its A T P pocket and inhibits it. A leukaemia cell does not get through a period without it. Normal cells do.
scenes.caption: The molecule that worked is called imatinib. It hit a short list of kinases, not hundreds. One of them is BCR-ABL. scenes.visual: One large kinase with a pocket; the imatinib wedge slides into the pocket and the kinase goes from always-on to off. Then two cell chips: leukaemia cell needs BCR-ABL, normal cell gets through a period without.

scenes.tts: Some patients in the early imatinib trials, mostly those with advanced disease, got well and then relapsed. In one laboratory, a scientist read the B C R A B L gene from their blood. In several patients, one D N A letter had changed. A C T had become A T T. That replaces threonine at position three fifteen with isoleucine.
scenes.caption: Some patients in the early imatinib trials, mostly those with advanced disease, got well and then relapsed. In one laboratory, a scientist read the BCR-ABL gene from their blood. In several patients, one DNA letter had changed. ACT had become ATT. That replaces threonine at position 315 with isoleucine.
scenes.visual: A blood sample reads out the gene; a strip of DNA letters ACT changes its middle letter to ATT; the residue chip Thr 315 turns into Ile 315.

scenes.tts: Threonine three fifteen is one of the contacts that hold imatinib in its pocket. Isoleucine is bulkier. It cannot make that contact. So the drug no longer binds. But the enzyme does not need this residue for its own reaction. The kinase keeps working.
scenes.caption: Threonine 315 is one of the contacts that hold imatinib in its pocket. Isoleucine is bulkier. It cannot make that contact. So the drug no longer binds. But the enzyme does not need this residue for its own reaction. The kinase keeps working.
scenes.visual: Zoom on the pocket: the drug wedge held by a small knob Thr 315. The knob swells to a bulky Ile 315, the drug is pushed out. The kinase then puts a phosphate badge on a substrate chip.
scenes.narration: Threonine 315 is one of the contacts that hold imatinib in its pocket. Isoleucine is bulkier. It cannot make that contact. So the drug no longer binds. But the enzyme does not need this residue for its own reaction. The kinase keeps working.

scenes.tts: A relapse looks like a failure of the idea. Read it as an experiment instead. To survive, the leukaemia changed the one position the drug depended on. It left the rest of the enzyme alone. That is strong evidence that the drug had been working through B C R A B L, and that the leukaemia still needed it.

scenes.visual: The word failure is replaced by experiment. The kinase: only the one position is lit as changed, the rest stays plain. Two conclusion lines appear: the drug worked through BCR-ABL; the leukaemia still needed it.

scenes.tts: The relapse also wrote the specification for the next drug: grip A B L without needing residue three fifteen. Ponatinib was built with a slim carbon-carbon triple bond where the isoleucine side chain sticks out. It inhibits the mutant kinase. Keep this rule. A relapse writes the specification for the next drug.

scenes.visual: The mutant pocket with bulky Ile 315. A specification label appears, then a new wedge, ponatinib, with a slim rod that passes the isoleucine and sits in the pocket; kinase goes off. The rule line appears.
